# Supplement Facts Check

> An independent, open-data audit of dose disclosure on gut-health supplement labels. Six binary criteria, 0-6 scale. Methodology v1.13, locked 2026-09-27. Sample: the top 30 of Amazon's Best Sellers in Probiotic Nutritional Supplements captured 09/26/2026; 18 pass the inclusion test, 12 are excluded as not gut-health-first, 0 undecided. All 18 eligible products are scored. Authored by Ryan Pepple, who owns a competing brand (CalmGut, operating as SHUVEN); author-owned products are scored separately and never ranked.

## Headline findings

- None of 18 publish a publicly accessible third-party certificate of analysis (criterion 5): https://supplementfactscheck.org/findings/public-third-party-certificate-of-analysis.html
- Just one of 18 discloses a dose inside the clinical trial range (criterion 4): https://supplementfactscheck.org/findings/dose-within-clinical-trial-range.html
- Only 7 of 18 disclose an exact amount for every active ingredient (criterion 1): https://supplementfactscheck.org/findings/exact-doses-disclosed.html
- 12 of 18 state the standardization percentage (criterion 2): https://supplementfactscheck.org/findings/standardization-percentage-stated.html
- 12 of 18 name every chemical form or probiotic strain (criterion 3): https://supplementfactscheck.org/findings/chemical-form-or-strain-named.html
- 12 of 18 state both serving size and servings per container (criterion 6): https://supplementfactscheck.org/findings/per-serving-amounts-complete.html

## Known limitations

- 14 of 35 dose-reference rows have no range set; each records why, and criterion 4 cannot be scored from them.
- Criterion 5 records a certificate of analysis as not publicly accessible when a documented search failed to find one. That is a negative finding, not a claim that none exists.
- Scores describe what a label discloses on the capture date. Nothing here was lab-tested, and no claim is made about whether a product works.
- Source problem, L-glutamine (free-form), PMID 39397201: UNRESOLVED: the subgroup statistic is printed as WMD -0.01 with 95% CI -0.10 to -0.08 (n=5 studies), an interval that excludes its own point estimate; full text gives no way to determine the correct figures. SEPARATE INCONSISTENCY: Table 1 defines duration subgroups as ≥4 weeks / <4 weeks, but the Discussion/Conclusion instead describe the significant effect as occurring in interventions "less than 2 weeks" -- a cutoff absent from the paper's own methodology. Flag this if this row is ever used for a duration-based judgment, not just dose.
